item.description:
507

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific (EP94):
An area of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands has become slightly better organized over the last
several hours. Environmental conditions appear conducive for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form late this week or early this weekend while the system drifts to
the northeast, before turning westward by early next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves
slowly west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Zelinsky
NNNN

item.description:

959 
WTPA32 PHFO 270232

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  59
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...LALA EXPECTED TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW IN ABOUT 36 HOURS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...36.4N 178.5W
ABOUT 550 MI...890 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 36.4 North, longitude 178.5 West. Lala is 
moving toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A 
north-northwestward motion is expected through Thursday, followed by 
a gradual bend toward the west-northwest on Thursday night and 
Friday. On the forecast track, Lala is expected to cross the 
International Date Line in about 30 to 36 hours.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, and 
Lala is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low Thursday 
night.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 59
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 270232
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  59
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026

Lala's convective state has remained fairly steady over the past 6 
hours, with convective bands wrapping around the north and west 
sides of the cyclone, indicating that westerly shear of 10-15 kt 
isn't affecting the cyclone very much at this time. Subjective 
Dvorak classifications from PHFO and JTWC range from 30-35 kt, while 
objective satellite estimates range from 45-56 kt. The initial 
intensity will remain 40 kt for this advisory.

Lala is inching toward the northwest, or 325 degrees at 4 kt. Weak 
high pressure ridging to the northeast of Lala will keep the cyclone 
on a slow north-northwestward track for the next 24 h, but as 
ridging strengthens to the north of Lala, a turn toward the 
west-northwest is expected in 36-48 h. Little change was made to the 
previous NHC track forecast for the first 48 h. The forecast was 
adjusted to the left, or southwest, of the previous forecast at hour 
60-72. The NHC forecast is in best agreement with the HFIP 
Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA).

Sea-surface temperatures along Lala's track should remain steady 
over the next 36 h between 23-24C while northwesterly wind shear is 
forecast to increase slightly over the next day or so. 200 mb 
temperatures will increase slightly over the next couple of days, 
leading to an atmosphere that is slightly more stable. Model 
guidance is in good agreement that Lala will gradually weaken, and 
the cyclone's winds should eventually fall below gale force around 
the same time it loses its convection, which should occur in about 
36 hours. This is also about the same time that Lala is forecast to 
cross the International Date Line, but there is some chance it could 
still be a tropical cyclone when it crosses into the Eastern 
Hemisphere.  The remnant low should gradually spin down and open up 
into a trough in 3 to 4 days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
